title: Investigation and Security Measures following Mobile Guardian App Breach
what_it_is: Investigation and Security Measures following Mobile Guardian App Breach

sections.label: Mobile Guardian breach questions
sections.summary: Questions ask why Mobile Guardian was used after an April 2024 breach, whether contingency plans existed, and how affected students are supported.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) why was Mobile Guardian's device management app continued to be used after its data security breach in April 2024 which caused the exfiltration of personal data of parents and staff from 127 schools; (b) whether contingency plans were instituted prior to the loss of Internet access and classroom materials from students’ personal learning devices in July 2024 and the cybersecurity incident causing students’ devices to be remotely wiped in August 2024; and (c) whether affected students are adequately supported.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education following the cybersecurity incident involving the Mobile Guardian application (a) what targeted support is being offered to affected students experiencing distress, particularly those with existing mental health conditions; (b) for students whose data is unrecoverable, how is the Ministry assisting them to prepare for their upcoming examinations and ensuring their access to adequate learning materials; and (c) whether examination grades for the affected students will be moderated this year.

sections.label: Device wipe data questions
sections.summary: Questions ask for updates on devices wiped in August 2024, unrecoverable data, exam impact, backups, and restoration for national exam students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether there is an update to the number of students in Singapore who had their devices wiped remotely as a result of the Mobile Guardian cybersecurity breach in August 2024 and, if so, how many; (b) how many students were unable to recover their data; (c) what impact did this incident have on these students’ preparation for weighted assessments and examinations; (d) whether the Ministry has any backups of students’ data; and (e) if not, why not.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether there is an update on the efforts to restore devices that are affected by the Mobile Guardian system glitch and cybersecurity breach; and (b) in particular, whether students taking their national examinations have all been able to restore their devices.

sections.label: August 2024 Mobile Guardian cyberattack
sections.summary: On 4 August, a cyberattack on Mobile Guardian remotely wiped iPads of global customers, including 13,000 school PLDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Five days later, on 4 August, Mobile Guardian suffered a cyberattack, which remotely wiped out the iPads of some of their global customers, including 13,000 PLDs in our schools or approximately 8% of devices used by our secondary school population.

sections.label: Affected PLD data loss
sections.summary: About one in six of the 13,000 affected PLDs lost some data, and under 5% could not recover all data due to no prior backup.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: About one in six of the 13,000 affected PLDs lost some degree of data and less than 5% were unable to recover all their data, as their devices had previously not been backed up.

sections.label: MOE ceases Mobile Guardian use
sections.summary: MOE will cease Mobile Guardian in all PLDs, take legal action, study alternative solutions, and use interim safety measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Due to this incident, MOE has decided to cease the use of Mobile Guardian in all PLDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: MOE has also taken legal actions against the relevant contractors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: MOE is currently studying options for an alternative DMA solution for iPad and Chromebook PLDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will work towards rolling out the new DMA solution by the new school year in January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Until the new DMA solution is in place, schools have instituted additional processes to ensure that the PLDs are used safely and responsibly during school hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: MOE has activated web filtering through the Google Admin Console or Chromebook PLDs and through Parents Gateway, shared instructions on how to activate Apple's built-in parental controls on iPads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This way, parents can set boundaries, like screen time, routines and restrict access to unsavoury sites.

sections.label: Re-installing DMA plan
sections.summary: A question asks MOE's plan forward, particularly whether students will be required to re-install a DMA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In light of the Mobile Guardian incident, what is MOE's plan moving forward, particularly, whether the Ministry is going to require or mandate students to re-install a DMA moving forward?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We would like to re-install a DMA for all devices and the reason is very simple.

sections.label: Parents adopt default DMA settings
sections.summary: About three quarters of all parents will adopt the baseline default settings of a DMA for the devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: By and large, about three quarters of all parents will adopt the baseline default settings of a DMA for the devices.

sections.label: Mobile Guardian forensic investigation
sections.summary: Mobile Guardian was asked to do the independent forensic investigation and MOE also did its own.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, we asked Mobile Guardian to do the independent forensic investigation and we also did our own.

sections.label: Back-ups of student device data
sections.summary: A question asks whether MOE took back-ups of data on student devices while Mobile Guardian was installed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Did MOE take back-ups of the data on student devices during the time that Mobile Guardian was installed?

sections.label: Penetration test patches and attack
sections.summary: Patches from penetration tests are implemented progressively, but whether they contributed to the cyber attack awaits the full forensic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The second one is that in any penetration test, be it the one in June or subsequent to it, whenever there is a penetration test and the results are found, then there will be a series of patches that will be implemented progressively to fix the issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Did any of this contribute directly or indirectly to the subsequent cyber attack?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I will not be able to comment on this at this point in time, until the full forensic is out.

sections.label: Students backing up notes on cloud
sections.summary: Most students backed up notes and information on the cloud and recovered most information, while a small percentage could not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will back up what we want in a smartphone, be it photos or notes, but it would not be that Apple will back up everything for us, unless you do an auto setting for everything to be backed up onto the cloud storage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is the reason why most of our students, the vast majority of our students have been able to back up their notes and information on the cloud, and most of them were able to recover most of the information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: There is only a very small percentage of students who were unable to recover data because they did not back up individually and those parts of the data were not backed up.

sections.label: No personal devices for primary schools
sections.summary: MOE has decided not to issue personal learning devices to all primary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the use of iPads and devices for primary school education, at this point in time, MOE has not made a decision to issue --- In fact, we have made a decision not to issue personal learning devices to all primary schools.

sections.label: National exam iPad adjustments
sections.summary: Fewer than 60 students needed special adjustments for national examinations because some subject preparation work was done on the iPad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: At the national level, for national examinations, the number of students where we need to make special adjustments because some of their work in preparation for the particular subject was done in the iPad, the numbers were less than 60.

sections.label: Regular app vulnerability testing
sections.summary: MOE states that vulnerability testing is carried out regularly at different tiers depending on the security level of the systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: And moving forward, will MOE ensure that such testing should be carried out on a regular basis for such apps?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I have said in my answer that depending on the security level of the different systems, we have different tiers of vulnerability testing regularly.
